source_cautions: 2.NBT.7.1 is a separate California-added requirement, not a replacement for 2.NBT.7; neither is duplicated here.
2.MD.7 includes California-added time relationships; already staged separately, excluded here.
Grade 2 2.G.1 footnote specifies direct/visual size comparisons rather than measurement.
These are author editorial paraphrases for source audit, not accepted standards, canonical equivalence or assessment/mastery authorization.

rows.author_mathematical_scope: Mentally add or subtract 10 or 100 to or from a given whole number from 100 through 900.
Explain why addition and subtraction strategies work using place value and properties of operations; explanations may use drawings or objects.
required_material_conditions: drawings or objects may support explanations

rows.author_mathematical_scope: Measure an object's length by choosing and using an appropriate length-measuring tool, such as a ruler, yardstick, meter stick, or measuring tape.
required_material_conditions: ruler, yardstick, meter stick or tape

rows.author_mathematical_scope: Measure the same object twice using two different-sized units of length and describe how the numerical measurements depend on the size of the chosen unit.
required_material_conditions: numerical measurements relate to unit size

rows.author_mathematical_scope: Estimate lengths using inches, feet, centimeters, and meters.
Measure to determine how much longer one object is than another and express the length difference in a standard unit.
Use addition and subtraction within 100 to solve word problems involving lengths given in the same units; drawings and equations with a symbol for an unknown may represent the problem.
required_material_conditions: drawings or equations with unknown symbol

rows.author_mathematical_scope: Represent whole numbers as lengths from 0 on an equally spaced number line diagram and represent whole-number sums and differences within 100 on that line.
required_material_conditions: whole numbers as lengths from zero

rows.author_mathematical_scope: Solve word problems involving dollar bills, quarters, dimes, nickels, and pennies, using dollar and cent symbols appropriately.
required_material_conditions: dollar bills and four named coins

rows.author_mathematical_scope: Generate measurement data from several objects measured to the nearest whole unit or repeated measurements of one object; display the data as a line plot with a horizontal scale marked in whole-number units.
required_material_conditions: several objects or repeated same-object measurements

rows.author_mathematical_scope: Draw a picture graph and single-unit-scale bar graph for a data set of up to four categories; solve simple put-together, take-apart, and compare problems using bar-graph information.

Recognize and draw shapes with specified attributes, including a specified number of angles or equal faces; identify triangles, quadrilaterals, pentagons, hexagons, and cubes. Compare size directly or visually, not by measuring.
required_material_conditions: triangles, quadrilaterals, pentagons, hexagons and cubes
size comparison directly or visually, not by measurement

rows.author_mathematical_scope: Partition a rectangle into rows and columns of equal-sized squares and count the squares to find the total.

Partition circles and rectangles into two, three, or four equal shares; describe shares as halves, thirds, and fourths and the whole as two halves, three thirds, or four fourths; recognize equal shares of identical wholes need not have the same shape.
required_material_conditions: equal shares of identical wholes may differ in shape
